# Exact finite regular-15 reference exclusion below thirteen struts

**Verified by actual local execution.** For the regular 15-gon, the equilibrium columns of the boundary cycle together with **any covering convex-thrackle forest having 8 through 12 internal struts** are linearly independent. Hence none of these particular reference frameworks has a nonzero equilibrium stress, of any signs.

This is a finite regular-reference statement. It makes no assertion for arbitrary conic spacing, all odd orders, equal-diameter realizability, or global diameter-minimizing packings.

| Struts | Covering forests | Dihedral orbits | Exact equilibrium rank |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 8 | 15 | 1 | 23 |
| 9 | 560 | 23 | 24 |
| 10 | 6,048 | 214 | 25 |
| 11 | 28,800 | 1,000 | 26 |
| 12 | 70,400 | 2,388 | 27 |

There are 105,823 candidate forests in 3,626 dihedral orbits. Every rank equals the total number `15+struts` of equilibrium columns.

## Finite certificate and its mathematical meaning

The code enumerates every pairwise crossing-or-common-endpoint clique of nonboundary diagonals of the requested size, imposes acyclicity by union-find, and retains exactly the graphs covering all fifteen labels. Each graph is produced once in increasing edge-index order. A polygon side cannot occur in any covering thrackle forest with two or more components: every other edge would have to meet one of that side's endpoints, connecting all nonisolated labels into its component. Thus excluding sides loses no eligible forest here.

Let `zeta=exp(2pi i/15)`. Replace usual regular coordinates by

    X_j=zeta^j+zeta^(-j),
    Y_j=zeta^j-zeta^(-j).

This is an invertible complex linear change of the regular cosine/sine coordinates, with a common nonzero scale if the rim is normalized to unit sides. Equilibrium rank is unchanged.

The transpose equilibrium matrix has `15+struts` rows and thirty columns, with entries in `Z[zeta]`. For every dihedral representative the JSON records a prime `p`, a primitive fifteenth root `z` in `F_p`, pivot-column indices of a full square minor, and the nonzero residue of its determinant. Dihedral rotations/reflections act by invertible coordinate changes and row/column permutations, including modulo these odd primes; consequently one representative certifies its entire orbit.

For primes not dividing fifteen, an element of exact multiplicative order fifteen is a root of the cyclotomic polynomial `Phi_15` modulo that prime. Evaluation `zeta -> z` therefore defines a ring homomorphism `Z[zeta] -> F_p`. A minor vanishing in `Z[zeta]` would also vanish under this homomorphism. Its certified nonzero residue proves that it is nonzero at the complex regular polygon, and hence proves the asserted real equilibrium independence.

The first prime/root pair was `p=31,z=9`; primality and exact order were checked by the executed code. It certified 3,569 orbits. **Fifty-seven remaining orbits had inconclusive rank loss modulo 31.** Every one was recovered by full rank modulo 61 at the independently checked order-fifteen root used in the JSON. No real dependence was inferred from a modular failure, and no exact-field recovery or stress-sign classification was needed.

The run completed successfully in approximately 63.4 seconds. The final data, including every orbit representative and modular minor witness, are in `erdos99-regular15-small-support-modular-exact.json`; the complete executable is `work/check-regular15-small-support-modular.py`. The similarly named partial JSON is a checkpoint, not an additional experiment.

## Attribution and limits

This is a focused native-agent extension of the complete worker410/root modular diagnostic. The code was reviewed and actually run locally. Dihedral caching and stored minor witnesses were added for this fifteen-vertex run. No historical novelty claim is made.

The consequence is only that a covering convex-thrackle forest supporting a nonzero stress **at this regular 15-gon** needs at least thirteen struts. The computation does not prove a general odd-order lower bound or any exclusion of all triangle-free global optimizers in Erdős Problem #99.

# Erdős Problem #99 — persistent research log

Started: 25 October 2026 (Europe/Brussels). Status: research in progress; no proof or disproof established.

Checked proofs are consolidated in [erdos99-verified-notes.md](erdos99-verified-notes.md). The work/erdos99 directory retains every worker prompt, bridge job ID, and raw result. 256 browser assignments have been acknowledged (251 completed, five failed); replacements aim for ten concurrent jobs when the bridge is available. As of27October the bridge is DEGRADED withzeroavailable slots, and257-266arepreparedbutunacknowledged. Three native reviewers are being used for bounded independent proof audits within the four-agent limit. No proof/disproof of the full eventual statement has been found.

## Target and verification standard

For n ≥ 2 let D_n be the least possible diameter of n points in the Euclidean plane with all mutual distances at least 1. Prove or disprove: there exists N such that every minimizer with n ≥ N contains an equilateral triangle with side length exactly 1.

A finite small-n exception does not disprove the statement. Approximate equilateral triangles, asymptotic triangular density, and near-optimal triangle-free configurations do not settle it. A disproof needs rigorously certified triangle-free global minimizers for unbounded n. Every proposed proof is provisional until independently checked.

## Sources and attribution ledger

- Paul Erdős, [*Some problems in number theory, combinatorics and combinatorial geometry*](https://mathematica-pannonica.ttk.pte.hu/articles/mp05-2/mp05-2-261-269.pdf), Math. Pannon. **5** (1994), 261–269, §3.2, p.268: original page visually inspected by root and several workers. The eventual universal statement and infinitely-many-n requirement for disproof are confirmed. The paragraph also distinguishes a large triangular-lattice intersection from total lattice containment.
- András Bezdek and Ferenc Fodor, *Minimal diameter of certain sets in the plane*, J. Combin. Theory Ser. A (1999), 105–111: source named by the problem site; full text not yet checked.
- T. F. Bloom, [Erdős Problem #99](https://www.erdosproblems.com/99), accessed 2026-10-25. Direct fetch returns HTTP 403. Search-indexed original-site forum and prize pages reproduce the statement and list it as open; this is evidence of the site's recorded status, not proof that no resolution exists.
- Archit Das, [*Stress, rigidity and rhombic reductions for an Erdos minimum-diameter problem (Problem #99)*](https://zenodo.org/records/22768362), 15 September 2026, DOI 10.5281/zenodo.22768362. Full 17-page PDF retrieved locally after first-wave web-only access failed. Root checked §§2–6 preliminarily; independent full-text audits of adapted stress, convex tilings, and lattice obstruction are running. Treat stronger results as attributed preprint claims until audits finish.
- Paul Bateman and Paul Erdős, [*Geometrical Extrema Suggested by a Lemma of Besicovitch*](https://renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1951-03.pdf), American Mathematical Monthly **58** (1951), 306–314, Theorem 3. Primary theorem statement inspected: D_7=2, uniquely attained by a unit regular hexagon and center. A full proof audit has not been performed here.
- Andriy Bondarenko, Douglas P. Hardin and Edward B. Saff, [*Minimal N-Point Diameters and f-Best-Packing Constants in R^d*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1204.4403), Proc. AMS **142** (2014), 981–988 (electronic publication 2013). Bibliography corrected by full-paper worker 20. Its reference led to the original Schürmann theorem.
- Achill Schürmann, [*On Extremal Finite Packings*](https://link.springer.com/content/pdf/10.1007/s00454-002-0747-6.pdf), Discrete Comput. Geom. **28** (2002), 389–403, Theorem 9. Worker 20 retrieved and audited the original full theorem: sufficiently large exact diameter minimizers are not subsets of an admissible packing lattice, uniformly over varying lattices. The infinite lattice must itself have minimum separation ≥1. This already removes the newer preprint's rigidity hypothesis in its full-lattice special case; no lattice-exclusion novelty is claimed here.

## Research orchestration

The installed WebAgentGPT bridge reported READY, extension connected and project configured, capacity 20, no active workers. Ten independent browser-worker assignments cover literature, Delaunay geometry, variational stress, density limits, counterexamples, computation, planar rhombi, adversarial audit, the 2026 preprint, and local replacement. Worker prompts and job identifiers are saved under work/erdos99/. Findings will be cross-shared through fresh bounded follow-up jobs. No worker output is automatically accepted as a proof.

## Attempt registry

| ID | Direction | Present status / next check |
|---|---|---|
| A01 | Current literature and exact original statement | Initial primary-site index found; full source audit pending. |
| A02 | Density forces an exact unit triangle | Unjustified as stated; explicit near-triangular triangle-free constructions sought. |
| A03 | Planar triangle-free contact graph forces flexibility | Unjustified as stated; boundary diameter constraints and stress signs must be included. |
| A04 | Rhombic lattice shear provides a counterexample | Near-optimality alone insufficient; global optimum certification required. |
| A05 | KKT/stress and boundary pinning | 2026 preprint found; independent audit pending. |

## Verified progress

### V01. A triangle-free restriction has the same infimum diameter, for every fixed n

Attribution: elementary argument developed by the root agent during this session; no novelty claim. Independent worker verification requested next.

Let A have minimum pairwise distance 1 and diameter D, and choose a unit pair. Rotate coordinates so this pair is horizontal. For t > 0 apply T_t(x,y) = (x,(1+t)y). For any difference vector (a,b), its new squared length is a²+(1+t)²b² ≥ a²+b². Thus all pair distances remain at least 1, and the chosen horizontal pair stays exactly 1. Equality to 1 after stretching is possible only for an originally unit horizontal difference. Consequently every unit edge of T_t(A) is horizontal, so there is no unit equilateral triangle. Also diam(T_t(A)) ≤ (1+t)D.

Taking A to be an optimizer shows that the infimum diameter among triangle-free, minimum-distance-1 n-point configurations equals D_n. The infimum need not be attained. This proves that a positive diameter gap between all triangle-free configurations and all configurations is impossible even for a fixed n. Any proof of #99 must use attainment or a strict local/global optimality property, rather than a uniform triangle-free density or diameter gap.

This does not settle #99: the construction generally increases diameter, however slightly.

### V02. Basic optimization formulation and stress normalization

Attribution: standard nonlinear optimization; an equilibrium stress is also claimed in Archit Das (2026). The following short derivation was checked directly here; no claim of novelty.

Use variables p_1,...,p_n and s = D². Minimize s subject to 1 − |p_i−p_j|² ≤ 0 and |p_i−p_j|² − s ≤ 0. At a feasible configuration with s > 0, the direction δp_i = p_i, δs = 2s+1 strictly decreases every active constraint: contact derivatives are −2 and diameter derivatives are −1. Thus MFCQ holds. At a minimizer there are nonnegative multipliers μ on unit pairs and λ on diametral pairs such that

Σ_diam λ = 1,
Σ_j μ_ij(p_i−p_j) = Σ_j λ_ij(p_i−p_j) for every i,
Σ_contact μ = D².

The last identity follows by dotting equilibrium with p_i and summing. This produces a stress, but does not establish positivity on every unit contact or any rigidity conclusion. Those extra assertions require proof.

## Research deductions and audit outcomes

### C01. A unique diametral pair would produce a triangle-free optimizer of the same size — route closed

Rotate a minimizer so its unique diametral pair is horizontal. A sufficiently small vertical stretch leaves this pair at distance D and all other pairs below D, since finitely many strict upper inequalities have positive slack. It stretches every nonhorizontal unit edge. If no horizontal unit edge existed, all distances would become >1; scaling down to minimum distance 1 would contradict optimality. Hence a horizontal unit edge exists, and a small vertical stretch preserves both minimum distance 1 and diameter D while leaving only horizontal unit edges. The resulting optimizer is triangle-free.

Initially the stress identity suggested an integer diameter and a straight unit chain. A stronger elementary argument below rules out this hypothesis entirely for diameter >1, so do not search again for an unbounded unique-diameter family without addressing that lemma.

### V03. Every local diameter minimum with D > 1 has at least two diametral pairs

Attribution: proof developed by root in this session; independent detailed mathematical verification by native agent `/root/audit_unique_diameter`. No literature novelty claim.

Suppose pq is the unique diametral pair. Rotate p=(0,0), q=(D,0) and perform a sufficiently small vertical stretch. It preserves diameter D, because pq stays fixed and all other finitely many upper inequalities retain strict slack. Every surviving unit edge is horizontal. If none survives, minimum separation becomes >1, and normalization strictly improves D. Otherwise unit-contact components are horizontal paths of consecutive unit steps, including isolated vertices.

If p,q lie in different components, translate p's entire component slightly toward q. Internal contacts stay unit; all pairs in different components have strict lower slack, and all other pairs have strict upper slack below D. Thus a sufficiently small translation decreases diameter.

If they lie in the same component, that entire component is a straight chain r_j=(j,0), j=0,...,k, with k=D≥2 an integer. It cannot extend beyond either endpoint, since that would exceed the diameter. Replace r_0 by (0,0), r_1 by (cos θ,sin θ), and r_j by (j−2+2cos θ,0) for 2≤j≤k. Consecutive links remain unit, all noncontact inequalities persist by finite strict slack, and the unique diameter becomes k−2+2cos θ<k. This again improves diameter.

Both modifications can be arbitrarily small, including the preliminary stretch, so the argument rules out a local minimum. The D>1 hypothesis is essential: two unit-separated points give a unique diameter at D=1. The proof also works for the exact-minimum-distance-1 formulation because unit contacts remain, or normalization restores them.

## Do not repeat without a new ingredient

- Density or compactness alone: blocked by V01, including generic perturbations with just one unit contact.
- Contact graph has fewer than 2n−3 edges, therefore diameter can shrink: false; the unit square supplies a rigorous small-n obstruction.
- KKT multipliers exist, therefore all contacts are stressed: unjustified. In the exact seven-point hexagon-and-center optimizer one valid stress has zero weight on all spokes, another on all hexagon sides.
- Near-circular rhombic patch plus arbitrary boundary pins: cannot substitute those pins for actual diametral endpoints.
- Complete affine hexagonal or rectangular patch: exact family optimality is not unrestricted optimality; both shapes have asymptotically inferior diameter constants.
- A diameter-essential deletion plus a vacancy: replacement is valid, but neither condition is known to hold in every large triangle-free optimizer.
- Purely affine improvement: blocked by worker 13's explicit Pell family of near-circular triangle-free patches with strict optimum over the entire affine family. Root found a non-affine quadratic velocity that improves that same family; independent audit pending.

## Later verified progress and active checks

- **V04: parallel contacts.** Worker 12 supplied a complete second-order perturbation proving that exclusively parallel unit edges cannot occur at a local diameter minimum with D>1. Root checked the formula; see verified notes §3.
- **V05: infinite density.** Worker 12 independently confirmed worker 04's bounded monotone-row deformation: no unit triangle despite exact optimal limiting infinite density. This is not a finite optimum. See verified notes §4.
- **V06: convex rhombic class.** Root/native audit gives the sharp local exclusion: only the unit square can be a triangle-free local diameter minimum whose points are the complete vertex set of a convex edge-to-edge unit-rhombus tiling. Browser worker 18 independently excluded every global case except the square via comparisons, and identified the minimum-separation omission in Das Lemma 7.1. Intended theorem unaffected because its packing hypothesis supplies the omitted assumption.
- **V07: adapted stress.** Full-paper browser worker 17 verified Das Theorem 1.2 and Lemmas 3.1–3.3, including one common adapted stress and m≥2s−6k. Root separately inspected the complete proofs. Co-large support s=n−O(sqrt(n)) remains unproved.
- **V08: two-direction bound.** Root/native audit proved D≤2k for an optimizer in a unit two-direction rhombic packing lattice, without active bar rigidity; a self-contained hull-vector count gives the coarse explicit D≤512π². Prior Schürmann theorem already supplies lattice exclusion. Extension of D≤2k to multiple real-coordinate translates is under browser audit.
- **V09: local traps.** Root's regular odd unit polygon boundaries filled with a slightly dilated triangular-lattice interior passed full native audit. Reinhardt's sharp perimeter bound certifies ordinary local minima, density approaches the global optimum, and most vertices are isolated rattlers. A separate packing comparison proves these are eventually NONglobal. See verified notes §7. Browser audit 28 also running. Local optimality cannot replace global optimality in a stress-coverage or density-gap theorem.
- **V10: Pell patches.** Worker 13's s²−3r²=−2 near-circular patches passed full browser-23 audit. They are strict affine-family optima, but root's quadratic even velocity opens every unit edge with unchanged diametral vectors, and normalization strictly improves them. Root reproduced all four reported cardinalities and verified an exact rational improvement for n=93. See verified notes §8. This closes these candidates as possible local or global counterexamples.
- **V11 (root checked, further audit assigned): accordion.** Worker 21 supplied a direct contact-preserving coordinate-accordion motion for arbitrary subsets of a two-direction packing lattice: if D>2(b−1), where b counts actual diametral ENDPOINTS, every diameter can be decreased while preserving all old unit links. Uniform hull counting excludes D≥5000 in this class even as ordinary local minima. Do not confuse endpoint count b with pair count k. Worker 31 is checking the proof and extension.
- **V12 (root checked, further audit assigned): stress confinement.** Worker 25 proved every positive contact-stress component lies in the convex hull Q of loaded diametral endpoints. For k=2, Q has area ≤D²/2, so Oler and the exact global comparison force at least (1−2/π)n−O(sqrt(n)) points outside Q, all unstressed under every KKT stress. Combining the contact-minimal locking result would make exterior points isolated rattlers. This is a necessary condition, not a contradiction; global replacement remains unproved. Worker 32 auditing.

The main question remains open here. Do not mark the goal complete or blocked just because these restricted arguments leave the global case unresolved.

## Continuation research checkpoint: assignments 24–48

The preceding turn made progress, not a no-progress wait: it added checked proofs, local exact computations and source audits. This continuation has read results24,26–38 and launched replacements35–48. All bridge jobs have succeeded so far; no duplicate submissions or failed attachment retries.

- **V13: maximal-contact selection.** Root's no-isolated-vertex selection lemma passed worker38 audit. It only selects ONE triangle-free global optimizer without rattlers if any exists. It does not remove rattlers from EVERY optimizer, and does not preserve minimum-contact locking. A cycle-rank lexicographic rule yields no isolates plus frozen cyclic contacts; bridges remain a gap. See verified notes §9.
- **V14: stress component refinement.** Worker36 independently checked worker26's maximal ALLKKT support/complementary critical-cone direction; this must not be confused with maximal ADAPTED support. It improved the component span to >(sqrt(2)−1)D and root's component count refinement gives m≥2s−4k. Co-large support remains unproved. See notes §10.
- **V15: real-coordinate two-direction geometry.** Worker29 verified D≤2k without common lattice containment when all contact vectors belong to two well-conditioned directions. It supplied D≤2k² in the acute-angle triangle-free forest case, yielding angle-independent k=Ω(n^(1/4)) for this restricted class. No exclusion of arbitrary two-direction component offsets follows yet.
- **V16: exact triangular lattice occupancy.** Root proposal/worker35 proof gives at least n/3−O(sqrt(n)) off-lattice points in every hypothetical triangle-free GLOBAL optimizer relative to every exact unit triangular lattice. Controlled low-interface grain decompositions also obey a deficit. This says nothing about near-lattice geometry or arbitrary many thin grains. See notes §11.
- **V17: finite-alphabet row accordion.** Root/native proof extends constructive local exclusion to specified nonlattice systems p_ij=U_i+j u, with q fixed step directions having a uniformly positive transverse projection. D>(q+1)(b−1) gives descent and the uniform hull count h=O(D^((q+1)/(q+2))) makes large local minima impossible. General three-direction domains need not have the representation; worker39 auditing that classification. See notes §12.
- **V18: off-lattice contact classification.** Worker37 proved off-lattice unit circles meet strict unit-rhombic lattices in at most two sites. Triangle-free double contacts exist iff |cosθ|≥1/4 and require two adjacent missing lattice sites. Root reproduced the enumeration and symbolic root exclusions using work/check-off-lattice-contacts.py. See notes §13; worker46 independently auditing overlapping witness/incidence consequences.
- **V19: defect-tolerant release (conditional).** Worker24 extended Schürmann-style triangular-lattice vacancy releases through SAFE interior sites (no defect unit contacts) to a safe diametral vertex cover. It gives an actual strict diameter improvement when its hypotheses hold. At most one triangular-lattice unit neighbor per off-lattice point was checked. O(D) boundary defects can still block all relevant boundary sites; there is no proof that every global optimizer has a safe release cover.
- **V20: local trap audit.** Worker28 independently confirmed notes §7, including unrestricted local minimality, all exact contacts, the density asymptotic, and eventual strict global nonoptimality. It supplied primary Reinhardt bibliography. Worker34 independently audited the first six note sections and found no mathematical error under the hypotheses. These are mathematical audits, not formal proof-assistant verification.
- **V21 (restricted): strict local traps.** Worker33 proved regular odd prime unit polygons are strict local minima with no rattlers via Reinhardt uniqueness. It supplied a Fourier/positive-stress rigidity proof for all odd orders. Root checked the mode calculation; these packings have D~n/π and are very far from global density. No dense strict local family is established. Worker42 is attempting a concrete frame-and-mesh construction.

### Quantified boundary-capacity gap, not a resolution

Worker30 analyzed a prescribed regular unit odd polygon boundary. Every point in a configuration with its own diameter L is within its circumdisk of radius R. Oler gives capacity M≤(2π/sqrt(3))R²+πR+1. A translated slightly dilated triangular lattice in the exact safe interior yields M≥(2π/sqrt(3))R²−αm−O(1), α=π/(3sqrt(3))−1/2≈0.1046. The global comparison threshold is T=πL²/(2sqrt(3)). Thus the sign of M−T remains undetermined at linear boundary order. The empty-strip examples cannot justify a universal capacity deficit. Workers40,41,43 now investigate surface coefficients, explicit capacity examples and sharper actual-diameter bounds.

### Do not repeat these additional failed inferences

- Maximal-contact no-rattler selection plus minimal-contact locking does not automatically describe the same optimizer.
- A low number of off-lattice vertices does not bound their total positive stress. Worker22 derived an explicit stress-error inequality containing exceptional stress masses; those terms cannot be dropped.
- Three contact directions do not force one containing packing lattice. Worker27 gave a connected zigzag grid with three directions and a subunit lattice difference obstruction; its specific rectangular examples improve by changing the zigzag parameter.
- The sharp n/3 lattice-occupancy deficit applies to EXACT unit triangular lattices, not arbitrarily slightly sheared/dilated lattices.
- Finite-alphabet row-translate coordinates are an explicit structural hypothesis. An arbitrary near-rhombic quadrangulation has not been reduced to that form.

# Reuleaux carrier capacity: a global restriction

This is a checked necessary condition for global optimality, not a solution of Erdős99. It counts every point, including contact isolates. No historical novelty is claimed.

Let a=pi/(2sqrt(3)). If an n-point unit-separated set P has globally minimum diameter D, then
\[
\boxed{n\ge aD^2+1.} \tag{1}
\]
To see the +1 directly, average a translated unit triangular lattice inside the OPEN disk of radius D/2. The mean count is aD^2. Every finite crop has diameter strictly below D, so every crop has at most n-1 points. Averaging gives (1). No strict monotonicity of the sequence D_n and no discrepancy theorem is used.

Suppose in addition that P is contained in a width-D Reuleaux polygon K with at most m genuine positive arcs, where m>=3 is odd. All these arcs have radius D. [Firey1960, Theorems1–2](https://msp.org/pjm/1960/10-3/pjm-v10-n3-p08-p.pdf), pp.823–824, gives
\[
|K|\le\frac{D^2}{2}\left(\pi-m\tan\frac\pi{2m}\right),
\qquad \operatorname{per}K=\pi D.
\]
The at-most-m statement follows by removing zero arcs and using the strict increase of regular area with odd arc count. Firey's correct pagination is Pacific Journal of Mathematics10(3)(1960),823–829, DOI10.2140/pjm.1960.10.823. The native circular reviewer checked the original theorem and formula; root read the primary paper and independently simplified the regular area formula. [Sallee1970](https://doi.org/10.4153/CMB-1970-037-1) supplies an alternative proof.

Apply [Oler's finite packing inequality](https://doi.org/10.1007/BF02559533) to the convex body K. With
\[
C_m=\frac{m\tan(\pi/(2m))-\pi/2}{\sqrt3}>0,
\]
it gives
\[
\boxed{n\le aD^2-C_mD^2+\frac\pi2D+1.} \tag{2}
\]
Combining (1) and (2),
\[
\boxed{D\le\frac\pi{2C_m}.} \tag{3}
\]
Since tan(x)>x+x^3/3 for x>0 in this range,
\[
C_m>\frac{\pi^3}{24\sqrt3 m^2},
\qquad
\boxed{m>\frac\pi{\sqrt{12\sqrt3}}\sqrt D
=0.6890947418\ldots\sqrt D.} \tag{4}
\]
Thus no fixed-arc Reuleaux carrier family can contain globally optimal packings with unbounded D.

If the separately checked stronger global inequality n>=aD^2+1+c0sqrt(D) is used, where c0=3^(5/4)/(128pi), then (2) yields the refinement
\[
m^2\ge\frac{\pi^3D^2}{24\sqrt3\,[\pi D/2-c_0\sqrt D]}.
\]
The elementary version (3)–(4) does not depend on that stronger input.

Every point of P lies in that intersection. Its m boundary arcs each subtend pi/m, and its area is the polygon area plus m circular segments. Writing alpha=pi/(2m) and R=D/(2cos(alpha)), this sum is
\[
\frac{mD^2\sin(4\alpha)}{8\cos^2\alpha}
+\frac{mD^2}{2}(2\alpha-\sin(2\alpha))
=\frac{D^2}{2}(\pi-m\tan\alpha).
\]

## Completion for every odd actual-diameter cycle

Let m=2s+1 selected diameter-cycle vertices be v_0,...,v_(m-1) in convex-hull order. They are strictly exposed: if |p-q|=D, then for any other point z,
\[
2(p-q)\cdot(z-p)\le-|z-p|^2<0.
\]
Two disjoint diameter edges cannot be noncrossing: they would be opposite sides of a strictly convex quadrilateral whose diagonal sum is strictly greater than 2D, although both diagonals are at most D.

The cycle must consequently be the usual convex odd star. For one of its edges, remove its two endpoints from the cycle. The remaining path alternates between the two sides of that chord, because its edges cross the selected edge. The two shores among the remaining 2s-1 vertices therefore have sizes s and s-1. Each cycle edge joins convex positions differing by s or s+1. Since every vertex has two cycle neighbors, these are exactly its two opposite positions. Thus
\[
|v_i-v_{i+s}|=|v_i-v_{i+s+1}|=D.
\]

Set K=intersection_i B(v_i,D). Consider the minor circular arc Gamma_j from a=v_j to b=v_(j+1), centered at c=v_(j+s+1), of radius D. The central angle is at most pi/3. On this circle another disk B(z,D) permits directions u satisfying
\[
u\cdot\frac{z-c}{|z-c|}\ge\frac{|z-c|}{2D}.
\]
This is an angular interval strictly shorter than pi. It contains the directions of a and b and therefore their minor arc. Hence Gamma_j lies in K and on its boundary; its relative interior lies strictly inside every other defining disk.

The center c lies on the interior side of the hull edge ab, so the minor arc lies on its exterior side and contains no other selected vertex. The boundary of convex K is a Jordan curve, with the selected vertices in hull order. Gamma_j is therefore their consecutive boundary portion: the other boundary portion contains the remaining m-2 vertices. All these arcs exhaust the boundary. Each has positive length and its disk is essential.

Let U_i be the outward-normal interval of the arc centered at v_i. The two arcs meeting at the vertex v_i have the opposite endpoint normals, so its corner normal interval is exactly -U_i. For u in U_i, the opposite supporting points are v_i+D u and v_i, at separation D. The intervals U_i and -U_i cover all directions, and width is symmetric under u->-u. Thus K has constant width D, exactly m positive radius-D arcs, and contains ALL of P.

Firey and (1)–(4) now apply to ANY odd actual-diameter cycle, without regularity. Any surviving odd cycle in a global minimizer has length greater than 0.6890947418sqrt(D); a forest diameter graph remains possible under this theorem. No unit-triangle conclusion follows.

# A sharp rhombus-defect budget retaining every point

Let P be a finite planar unit-separated set, n=|P|, C=conv(P), diameter D. Suppose Q_1,...,Q_q are empty unit rhombi with disjoint interiors, appearing as faces of a plane unit-contact graph. Put a0=sqrt(3)/2 and
\[
E=\sum_i(|Q_i|-a_0).
\]
Unit separation forces each acute rhombus angle to be at least60 degrees, so E>=0. An extra packing point cannot lie inside a unit rhombus: its two shorter-diagonal triangles have circumradius at most1/sqrt(2), giving a vertex strictly closer than one to every interior point.

The finite inequality is
\[
\boxed{n+E/a_0\le |C|/a_0+\operatorname{per}(C)/2+1.} \tag{1}
\]
There is no bound or restriction on the number of contact isolates in this statement.

## Exact complex accounting

The primary tool is [Folkman–Graham1969, §3, printedp.746](https://www.cambridge.org/core/services/aop-cambridge-core/content/view/745BF5B96E3285103D53BCCE5D5B08AD/S000843950005428Xa.pdf/a-packing-inequality-for-compact-convex-subsets-of-the-plane.pdf). For any finite planar simplicial complex K with unit-separated vertices,
\[
V(K)\le A(K)/a_0+P_{\rm FG}(K)/2+\chi(K),
\quad
P_{\rm FG}(K)=\sum_e(2-\nu_e)|e|,
\]
where nu_e is the number of incident triangular faces. Boundary edges count once, bare edges twice, and internal seams zero times. Disconnected complexes, holes and isolated vertices are allowed. The native circular reviewer downloaded and visually checked the theorem and definition in the original scan.

Triangulate C using ALL n packing points and the chosen unit-contact edges, placing one diagonal inside every Q_i. No additional vertices are needed. Remove the two triangles and their common diagonal in each rhombus. KEEP all vertices and every other edge, including bare edges between two removed rhombi. Then
\[
V(K)=n,\quad\chi(K)=1-q,\quad

\]

In particular, $h\geq D$ and $z=0$ force $M=\Omega(D^{1/3})$. Different classes need not have the same orientation.

For an endpoint $a$, choose a diameter partner $b$. For every other point $x$, expanding $|x-b|^2\leq|a-b|^2$ gives

\[
(a-b)\cdot(a-x)\geq |a-x|^2/2\geq1/2.
\]

Write (q$a$) for the approximating lattice site. For another endpoint $x$ in the same class,

\[

\]

\]

# A weighted stress-orientation inequality

This checked conditional obstruction gives no uniform stress bound and no global competitor.

For normalized physical equilibrium, write unit-edge directions theta_e, diameter directions phi_f, and
\[
Z=\sum_f\lambda_f e^{2i\phi_f},\quad A=|Z|.
\]
Tensor equilibrium and its trace give
\[
\sum_e\mu_e=D^2,\qquad
\sum_e\mu_e e^{2i\theta_e}=D^2Z.
\]
Let c_e be the number of incident unit-rhombus faces, W0=sum_(c_e=0)mu_e, and W_Q=sum_(e on Q)mu_e/c_e. For each rhombus choose its ACUTE bisector beta_Q; at a square either perpendicular bisector works. Let e_Q=sin(alpha_Q)-sqrt(3)/2. For any common physical direction beta, let d_Q be angular distance modulo pi, NOT modulo pi/2.

Then
\[
\boxed{A+\frac2{D^2}\sum_QW_Q\sin d_Q
\ge\frac12-\frac{3W_0}{2D^2}
-\frac{2+\sqrt3}{D^2}\sum_QW_Qe_Q.}
\]

Indeed z_Q=sum_(e on Q)(mu_e/c_e)exp(2i theta_e) has real projection W_Q cos(alpha_Q) in its own bisector direction, regardless of unequal weights. Concavity of sqrt(1-x^2) for x in[sqrt(3)/2,1] gives cos(alpha)>=1/2-(2+sqrt(3))e_Q. Changing bisector costs at most2W_Q sin(d_Q); nonrhombus edges cost at mostW0. Sum, using sum_QW_Q=D^2-W0, to obtain the formula.

For selected global cores let M=max_e mu_e. The facial budgets imply W0<=6piMD, while W_Q<=4M and the sharp FG bound gives sum e_Q<=sqrt(3)piD/4. Hence
\[
\boxed{A+\frac2{D^2}\sum_QW_Q\sin d_Q
\ge\frac12-\pi(12+2\sqrt3)M/D.}
\]
Thus if M=o(D) AND stress-weighted orientation dispersion is o(D^2), diameter-load anisotropy is at least1/2 asymptotically. Neither extra premise is proved, and a near-round hull does not imply uniform load weights or A=o(1).

# A conditional classification of positive contact trees

26 October 2026. This is a checked partial result, not a solution of [Erdős Problem 99](https://www.erdosproblems.com/99). No literature novelty or priority is claimed.

Let \(P\) be a finite unit-separated planar set of diameter \(D>1\). Suppose symmetric nonnegative weights satisfy
\[
\sum_{q:\,|p-q|=D}\lambda_{pq}(p-q)
=\sum_{r:\,|p-r|=1}\mu_{pr}(p-r)
\]
at every point, with some diameter weight positive. Let \(T\) denote the ENTIRE graph of strictly positive contact weights and \(S\) the endpoints of strictly positive diameter weights.

Assume \(T\) is a connected tree and every positively weighted diameter midpoint lies in \(\overline B_\delta(0)\), where
\[
0\le\delta<1/4.
\]

**Theorem.** The positive support has one of two shapes:

1. A straight unit-spaced path of integer length \(D\), whose endpoints are the only points of \(S\).
2. A star with four or six straight arms of the same positive integer length \(L\). Here \(D=2L\), all points of \(S\) are the leaves, and every positively weighted diameter joins opposite leaves about the sole branch \(v\). Every positive midpoint is exactly \(v\), so \(|v|\le\delta\).

If the FULL unit-contact graph is triangle-free, the star has four arms. Then in both cases
\[
\operatorname{area}(\operatorname{conv}S)\le D^2/2.
\]
This bounds the positive support hull, not the full packing hull. No full-contact-forest, local-minimum or global-minimum assumption is made.

## Preliminary geometry

Every actual diameter endpoint \(p\), with partner \(q\), is exposed in the full hull: for every \(x\ne p\),
\[
(p-q)\cdot(x-p)\le-\tfrac12|x-p|^2<0.
\]
In particular a diameter endpoint cannot lie strictly between two other packing points.

Outward diameter vectors at one point have pairwise angles at most \(60^\circ\), so their positive resultant cannot vanish. Thus \(S\subseteq V(T)\). Every leaf of \(T\) is loaded, since a single nonzero contact force cannot balance zero diameter load. At every unloaded degree-two vertex, the two unit contact directions are opposite and their positive weights equal.

The positive diameter graph is a matching. If \(p\) had two distinct positive partners \(q,q'\), their midpoints in \(\overline B_\delta(0)\) would give
\[
|q-q'|\le4\delta<1.
\]
Write the unique partner of \(p\in S\) as \(p^*\), and put
\[
R=D/2,\qquad a_p=(p+p^*)/2,\qquad
e_p=(p-p^*)/D.
\]
Then \(p=a_p+Re_p\), \(|a_p|\le\delta\), and \(|e_p|=1\).

For later separation arguments, a packing point \(z\) not incident to a unit segment \([a,b]\) satisfies
\[
|z-((1-t)a+tb)|^2
=(1-t)|z-a|^2+t|z-b|^2-t(1-t)\ge3/4.
\]
Hence its distance from that segment is at least \(\sqrt3/2\). Unit contact edges cannot cross properly. For two disjoint segments a closest pair can be chosen with one endpoint, including the parallel case. Therefore two geometric contact subtrees with disjoint vertex sets have distance at least \(\sqrt3/2\).

## A leaf stem saturates at its diameter partner

Take a tree leaf \(p\), with unique positive partner \(q\) and weight \(\lambda_{pq}>0\). Its contact goes toward \(q\), with weight \(D\lambda_{pq}\).

Follow the tree through unloaded degree-two vertices until its first loaded vertex or first branch. All traversed edges are straight, equally stressed unit segments. If that first exceptional vertex \(r\) is loaded, then
\[
r=p-me,\qquad e=(p-q)/D,\quad m\in\mathbb Z_{>0}.
\]
The diameter gives \(m\le D\). Exposedness prohibits \(0<m<D\), because \(r\) would lie strictly inside \([p,q]\). Thus \(r=q\), \(m=D\), and \(D\) is an integer.

The incoming contact force at \(q\) already equals its entire positive diameter load, since matching makes \(p\) its sole positive partner. Additional positive contact forces cannot sum to zero: an exposing normal at \(q\) has strictly positive dot product with each outward contact vector. Consequently \(q\) is terminal and connectedness makes the whole tree this straight path.

Thus the path case is proved. In a branching tree, every leaf-to-first-branch arm is straight, has unloaded interior, and ends at an unloaded branch. A loaded first branch would have triggered the same saturation contradiction.

## At most one branch

At a terminal branch of the suppressed branching tree, choose two leaf arms. For arm \(i\), with integer length \(L_i\),
\[
p_i=v+L_i e_i=a_i+Re_i,\qquad
v=a_i+(R-L_i)e_i.
\]
Its immediate neighbor toward the leaf is \(v+e_i\).

If \(|v|>2\delta\), neither coefficient \(R-L_i\) is zero. Two arms with the SAME sign of this coefficient are impossible. Indeed, their directions, or both negatives, lie in the cone subtended by \(\overline B_\delta(0)\) from \(v\). Its width is
\[
2\arcsin(\delta/|v|)<60^\circ,
\]
so their immediate unit neighbors would be less than one apart.

The two chosen arms must therefore have opposite signs. The arm with \(R-L_i<0\) passes through \(a_i\in\overline B_\delta(0)\) before reaching \(v\).

Each terminal two-leaf subtree consequently contains either:

- A: its branch vertex in \(\overline B_{2\delta}(0)\); or
- B: a point of one of its unit-edge arms in \(\overline B_\delta(0)\).

If there were two or more branches, the suppressed branching tree would have two terminal branches and hence two vertex-disjoint such subtrees. All pairings are impossible:

- AA: the two branch vertices would be at distance at most \(4\delta<1\).
- AB: a vertex and a nonincident unit segment would have distance at most \(3\delta<3/4<\sqrt3/2\).
- BB: their segment unions would have distance at most \(2\delta<1/2<\sqrt3/2\).

Thus there is at most one branch.

## Exact star geometry

Suppose there is one branch \(v\), with at least three arms. All arms are the straight leaf arms just described. If \(|v|>2\delta\), sign pigeonhole would give two arms of the same sign, contradicting the cone argument. Hence \(|v|\le2\delta\).

The branch is unloaded by saturation along any leaf arm. All other nonleaf vertices are unloaded degree two, so \(S\) consists exactly of the leaves.

For a leaf \(p=v+L_i e_i\), equilibrium places its positive partner at
\[
q=p-De_i=v+(L_i-D)e_i.
\]
Since \(q\) is another leaf, it must be on an opposite arm. A same-ray partner would require two distinct arms with the same immediate neighbor. Thus the arms pair antipodally, with integer lengths \(L_i,L_i'>0\) and
\[
L_i+L_i'=D,\qquad
m_i=(p+q)/2=v+b_i e_i,\qquad
b_i=(L_i-L_i')/2\in\tfrac12\mathbb Z.
\]

There are at least two distinct arm pairs. Suppose one imbalance \(b_i\) is nonzero, so \(|b_i|\ge1/2\). Compare another pair \(j\).

If \(b_j=0\), then \(|m_i-m_j|=|b_i|\ge1/2\). If \(b_j\ne0\), absorb each sign into its actual arm direction. These distinct directions differ by at least \(60^\circ\), by separation of the immediate unit neighbors. For lengths \(A,B\ge1/2\),
\[
A^2+B^2-2AB\cos\theta
\ge(A-B)^2+AB\ge1/4.
\]
Again \(|m_i-m_j|\ge1/2\).

Both cases contradict \(|m_i-m_j|\le2\delta<1/2\). Therefore every imbalance vanishes:
\[
L_i=L_i'=D/2=L\in\mathbb Z_{>0}.
\]
All positive midpoints equal \(v\), improving its bound to \(|v|\le\delta\).

The immediate neighbors of \(v\) have pairwise angular gaps at least \(60^\circ\), so there are at most six arms. Antipodal pairing makes their number even; branching gives four or six. Six forces unit triangles at \(v\), hence is excluded by full triangle-freeness.

The path hull has zero area. For four arms the leaf hull is a quadrilateral with both diagonals of length \(D\), so its area is at most \(D^2/2\).

The native unique-diameter auditor independently verified every step, including \(\delta=0\) and the strict endpoint exclusion. Worker 186 independently checked the complete quarter-range theorem and supplied an alternative endpoint-variance proof of the AA/AB/BB separation step.

The equilibrium and harmonic maximum-principle tools are classical; general background is [Connelly–Whiteley (1996)](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~connelly/pdf/10.1137_S0895480192229236.pdf). No assertion of novelty or publication priority is made.

The endpoint \(\delta=1/4\) is outside this proof's strict matching and separation inequalities; no sharpness claim is made. The available global-optimizer midpoint bounds grow with \(D\) and do not supply the absolute hypothesis here. Zero-stress points can also enlarge the full hull. The original eventual unit-triangle problem therefore remains unresolved.

# Audit: three anchors and four terminal paths in a triangle-free positive core

Date: 28 October 2026. Input: worker331 response in `w42_331_three_terminal_unloaded_network.result.json`. Verdict: the classification and the stated unloaded-cycle Menger consequence are correct under the explicit hypotheses below. No general three-connectivity, cardinality bound, or asymptotic Erdős #99 conclusion follows here.

## Primary geometric input and exact scope

David Eppstein, *Edge Bounds and Degeneracy of Triangle-Free Penny Graphs and Squaregraphs*, Journal of Graph Algorithms and Applications 22(3) (2018), 483–499, DOI https://doi.org/10.7155/jgaa.00463.

Primary PDF: https://www.maths.tcd.ie/EMIS/journals/JGAA/accepted/2018/463.pdf.

Lemma 1, pp.487–489, gives four degree-two vertices in a biconnected triangle-free penny graph. Lemma 2, p.489, gives four distinct non-articulation vertices of degree at most two whenever a triangle-free penny graph contains a cycle. Its statement has no connectedness hypothesis. For a disconnected graph, apply the argument within a cyclic connected component; its degrees and articulation status are unaffected by other components.

The block-tree proof is sound: choose a cyclic block and its four degree-two vertices. A vertex that is not low-degree in the whole component leads through an attached branch to a leaf or leaf cyclic block, supplying a low-degree non-articulation vertex. Branches at different vertices cannot rejoin outside the chosen block, so the four supplied vertices remain distinct. Only the degree conclusion is needed below.

Saved original: `audit-eppstein2018-463.pdf`. Printed p.489 was visually inspected and saved as `audit-eppstein2018-p489.png`.

## Precise three-anchor proposition

Let P={p_1,...,p_r} be a finite planar point set with all pairwise distances at least one. Let F be its FULL unit-distance graph and H its FULL diameter graph. Suppose F is triangle-free, the bar rigidity matrix of F union H has rank 2r-3, and the framework has at least three noncollinear points.

Let T be a set of unit edges carrying strictly positive weights mu_e. Let U be a nonempty set of vertices satisfying:

1. Every u in U is incident to at least one edge of T.
2. No u in U is incident to an actual diameter edge in H.
3. At every u in U there is pure unit equilibrium:

       sum_{uw in T} mu_uw (p_w-p_u) = 0.

4. There is B disjoint from U, |B|<=3, such that EVERY F-neighbor of U outside U belongs to B. This includes zero-stress unit contacts.

Then K=F[U union B] is a forest. In fact U={u}, B has exactly three vertices, and K is precisely the three-spoke star centered at u.

## Proof, including the rank step

Full-contact closure makes the degree of each u in K equal to its degree in the full F. Positive incidence and equilibrium exclude degree zero and degree one.

If the full F-degree of u were two, its two neighbors a,b would both have positive weight, since one positive unit vector cannot balance. Equilibrium and equality of the two lengths imply equal weights and p_a-p_u=-(p_b-p_u). Assign a nonzero velocity perpendicular to line ab to u, and zero velocity to every other point. This preserves to first order every incident unit bar and, by the absence of diameter incidence, every diameter bar. All other bar constraints are unchanged.

This velocity is not an infinitesimal Euclidean rigid motion: it fixes the two distinct points a,b, whereas any infinitesimal rigid motion fixing two distinct points is zero everywhere. It contradicts rank 2r-3. Therefore every u in U has K-degree at least three.

K is an induced full contact graph of a subset of P, so it is itself a triangle-free penny graph. If K contained a cycle, Eppstein's Lemma 2 would give four distinct vertices of K of degree at most two. None belongs to U; all four would belong to B, impossible. Thus K is a forest.

For any nontrivial tree component Q of K, the number L of leaves is

    L = 2 + sum_{v in Q, deg_Q(v)>=3} (deg_Q(v)-2).

Any component meeting U is nontrivial, all its leaves lie in B, and it needs at least three such leaves. Two U vertices in one component would require at least four leaves. Two distinct components meeting U would together need at least six distinct B leaves. Since |B|<=3, there is exactly one U vertex, in one component, and its degree is exactly three. Its three distinct neighbors exhaust B. No B-B edge is possible because K is a forest (also each would create a triangle with u). Thus K is exactly the star.

This classifies FULL contacts, not which spokes have positive weight. All three positive weights imply that u lies strictly inside the anchor triangle. If only two spokes have positive weight, those two must be opposite, and the third full contact can have zero weight.

## Four-terminal path consequence, with endpoint separators handled

Assume V is a set of vertices of the ambient rigid framework such that:

- every v in V is incident to positive unit stress;
- V is closed under FULL unit contacts: N_F(V) is contained in V;
- the pure unit equilibrium equation holds at every v in V minus S;
- S is a subset of V containing EVERY v in V incident to any actual diameter edge, including edges of zero diameter-stress weight.

Alternatively, take the framework on V itself as the ambient framework of the proposition, with its own full mixed rank and corresponding hypotheses. Global mixed rigidity does not automatically imply full rank of an arbitrarily restricted core; this implication is not used or asserted.

For every cycle C in F[V minus S], there are at least four pairwise vertex-disjoint C-to-S paths in F[V], with distinct start vertices on C and distinct end vertices in S. Paths can be shortened so their internal vertices lie outside C union S.

Suppose there are fewer than four. The set version of vertex Menger, with unit vertex capacities INCLUDING the source and terminal sets, gives a set B of at most three vertices meeting every C-to-S path. This convention permits B to meet C or S; it is essential because the conclusion requires distinct endpoints.

Delete B and let U be the union of all connected components of F[V]-B that meet C-B. Triangle-freeness gives |C|>=4, so C-B is nonempty and U is nonempty. No vertex of S-B lies in U, or a path avoiding B would connect C-B to S-B. Hence U is disjoint from S and has no actual diameter incidence.

Every vertex of U is incident to positive unit stress because U is contained in V. Every full unit neighbor of U lies in V by contact closure. In F[V]-B such a neighbor is in the same component, so any full unit neighbor outside U lies in B. Thus the three-anchor proposition applies.

Every vertex of C is in U union B. Since the graph in the proposition is FULLY induced, every edge of C is still present in F[U union B], including any cycle edges whose two endpoints lie in B. This contradicts the forest conclusion. It handles separators meeting either endpoint set without requiring any replacement or disjointness assumption on B.

## Exact failure modes and attribution

The argument needs full contact closure, not merely closure of the positive support T. For example, u=(0,0) can have two positive horizontal contacts at (+/-1,0) and a zero-weight full contact at (0,1). The horizontal weights balance, but the extra full bar blocks the transverse motion used in the degree-two argument. This local example explains the missing inference; it is not asserted as a complete counterexample satisfying every global hypothesis.

Every vertex of V being positively incident is also necessary for this proof. Merely adjoining arbitrary zero-stress vertices to a core does not give the degree-at-least-three conclusion for U. All actual diameter incidence must be marked in S; positive diameter-support endpoints alone are not the stated hypothesis.

No four-terminal property for T is proved. No connectivity statement for an individual unloaded vertex is proved: a three-spoke star is expressly allowed. A cycle in F[V] that contains S is outside the stated corollary.

Attribution: Eppstein's published Lemmas 1–2 provide the geometric low-degree theorem. Menger's theorem provides the path/separator duality. Worker331 proposed their combination with equilibrium and full mixed rank; this note independently checks and makes its hypotheses explicit. No claim of priority or resolution of Erdős #99 is made.

# Audit: strictly convex triangle-free unit pentagons with vanishing face slack

**Verdict: PASS.** Worker451's construction is valid. All five sides are exactly unit, all five diagonals are strictly greater than one for sufficiently small positive parameter, every turn is strictly convex, and the face slack tends to zero from above. This is a geometric counterexample to a uniform positive slack charge per empty triangle-free pentagonal unit face. It is not a stressed-core or local/global-minimum construction.

## 1. Exact construction and circle intersection

Put `a=sqrt(3)/2`, and let

    A=(0,0), B=(1,0), C=(3/2,a), q=t^2,
    D=C+(cos(2pi/3+q),sin(2pi/3+q)),
    L=|D|, h=sqrt(1-L^2/4),
    E=D/2+(h/L) J D,

where `J(x,y)=(-y,x)` and `t>0` is sufficiently small. In coordinates,

    D_x=3/2-(1/2)cos(q)-a sin(q),
    D_y=a+a cos(q)-(1/2)sin(q).

The construction has the useful EXACT identity

    L^2=4-4a sin(q),  h^2=a sin(q).                  (1)

For `0<q<pi`, this makes `h>0` and `0<L<2`; positivity of `L^2` follows from `a<1`. Thus the specified circle intersection exists. As `t->0+`,

    D=(1,2a)+t^2(-a,-1/2)+O(t^4),
    h=sqrt(a)t+O(t^5),
    E=(1/2,a)+sqrt(a)t(-a,1/2)+O(t^2).              (2)

The worker's weaker error estimates are valid. The positive square root in (1) gives the stated sign in (2).

## 2. Exact unit sides and all five diagonal signs

The lengths `AB=BC=CD=1` hold directly from their definitions. Since `D` is perpendicular to `JD`,

    |E|^2=L^2/4+h^2=1,
    |E-D|^2=L^2/4+h^2=1.

Thus `EA=DE=1` exactly.

The pentagon's five diagonals are precisely `AC,AD,BD,BE,CE`. The first three have squared limits

    |AC|^2=3, |AD|^2->4, |BD|^2->3,

so they remain strictly greater than one for small positive `t`.

For the two delicate diagonals, put `E_0=(1/2,a)` and `n=(-a,1/2)`. Their initial direction products are

    (E_0-B) dot n=a,
    (E_0-C) dot n=a.

Using (2), and keeping `B,C` fixed, gives

    |BE|^2=1+2a sqrt(a)t+O(t^2),
    |CE|^2=1+2a sqrt(a)t+O(t^2).

Both linear coefficients are strictly positive. Therefore both diagonals exceed one for all sufficiently small positive `t`. This verifies EVERY nonadjacent pair, including the two that become additional unit contacts at the limit. The FULL unit graph on the five labels is exactly the chordless cycle `C_5`, hence is triangle-free.

## 3. Simplicity and strict convexity

At `t=0` the vertices are

    A=(0,0), B=(1,0), C=(3/2,a),
    D_0=(1,2a), E_0=(1/2,a).

This is a simple weakly convex polygon: `E_0` is strictly inside the side `D_0 A` of the convex quadrilateral `ABCD_0`. Each pair of NONADJACENT boundary segments is disjoint at the limit and therefore has positive distance, since the segments are compact. Their finitely many positive separations persist under small perturbations. Adjacent segments have unit lengths, distinct endpoints, and, by the turn computation below, do not overlap. Hence the perturbed polygon is simple.

Four of its five successive turn determinants have limit `a>0`:

    [AB,BC], [BC,CD], [CD,DE], [EA,AB].

They remain positive for sufficiently small `t`. The fifth has the exact value

    [DE,EA]=[D,E]=Lh>0.

Thus the simple polygon has every successive turn strictly counterclockwise and is strictly convex. This supplies an explicit justification of simplicity rather than relying only on a visual statement that `E` moves outward.

Choose the packing to consist of these five vertices. Its full contact graph is the planar `C_5`, so the pentagonal interior is an empty bounded face of that chosen packing. "Empty" here means that no chosen packing label lies in its interior; no claim about saturation by all possible additional points is needed or made.

## 4. Exact area and slack asymptotic

The shoelace formula yields

    Area(ABCDE)=(1/2)([B,C]+[C,D]+[D,E]).

Direct calculation gives `[B,C]=a`, `[C,D]=2a cos(q)`, and `[D,E]=Lh`. Consequently there is an exact expression

    Area(ABCDE)=a/2+a cos(q)
                 +sqrt(a sin(q)(1-a sin(q))).        (3)

For small positive `t`, with `q=t^2`, this gives in particular

    Area(ABCDE)=3a/2+sqrt(a)t+O(t^3).

Thus the weaker worker expansion with an `O(t^2)` remainder is correct. More precisely, the first terms are

    Area(ABCDE)=3a/2+sqrt(a)t
                 -(a sqrt(a)/2)t^3-(a/2)t^4+O(t^5).

With no interior packing labels, the face slack is

    sigma=Area/a-5/2+1=Area/a-3/2
         =t/sqrt(a)+O(t^3).                          (4)

Its leading coefficient is positive. Hence `sigma>0` for every sufficiently small positive `t`, and `sigma->0` as `t->0+`. For every prescribed positive epsilon one can choose such a `t` with `0<sigma<epsilon`.

The limit itself has a flat corner and the extra unit diagonals `BE,CE`; it is not a triangle-free pentagonal face. Every sufficiently small POSITIVE parameter, however, has all the required strict properties. There is therefore no illicit use of a degenerate member as the actual counterexample.

## Scope and attribution

Root supplied the limiting triangular-lattice configuration; worker451 supplied the explicit circle-intersection perturbation and its verification. This focused audit checks those facts and adds the exact identities (1) and (3) and an explicit simplicity argument. No historical priority is claimed. The example only defeats a uniform geometric positive slack per such pentagon; it does not show these faces occur in an ordinary local minimum, a positive-stress selected core, or a global diameter minimizer, and it does not solve Erdos99.

# Universal stress positivity, finite release, and the forest obstruction

This document records independently checked partial results for Erdős Problem 99. It does not settle the eventual unit-triangle conjecture. The universal positivity and finite-release arguments were located in the public research repository [1337isnot1337/erdos-99, C53 restoration, 9 September 2026](https://github.com/1337isnot1337/erdos-99/blob/main/docs/reports/target_c_c53_orientation_and_ci_restoration_2026-09-09.md), §§2–6. That report is marked unreviewed; the proofs below were checked independently rather than accepted from that label. No novelty or priority is claimed.

## 1. Statement and conventions

Let P be a finite planar set with pairwise distances at least 1 and diameter D>1. A normalized physical stress is a pair of nonnegative weight systems satisfying
\[
\sum_{q:|p-q|=D}\lambda_{pq}(p-q)
=\sum_{r:|p-r|=1}\mu_{pr}(p-r),\qquad \sum\lambda=1.
\]
Let B and A be the weighted Laplacians of the positive unit contacts and positive diameter pairs, respectively. Then
\[
\boxed{\Omega=B-A\succeq0.}
\]
Equivalently, every planar velocity field satisfies
\[
Q(v)=\sum_D\lambda_{ij}|v_i-v_j|^2
-\sum_F\mu_{ij}|v_i-v_j|^2\le0.
\]
This assertion concerns every physical stress, not one selected certificate. It needs no local or global optimality, triangle-free hypothesis, or contact-forest hypothesis.

We use the previously checked positive-support facts recorded in verified notes §19: positive contacts form one connected component T containing all positively loaded endpoints S, and T lies in conv(S). Every diameter endpoint is strictly exposed, and unit-contact segments are planar. Thus, when S spans the plane, T is a connected circular-planar positive network with exposed terminals S in their convex order. Vertices outside T have zero stress rows.

## 2. Circular-planar resistance splits

Eliminate the nonterminal vertices of B. Its Dirichlet block is positive definite, and the resulting terminal response matrix Lambda is a positive Laplacian, invertible on the complement of constants. Write R=Lambda^+.

[Forcey (2021), Theorems 4.2 and 3.7](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2108.00550), imply that the effective-resistance metric of a connected circular-planar network has the form
\[
W=\sum_C w_C\,\delta_C,\qquad w_C\ge0,
\]
where C ranges over circular intervals of terminals and delta_C is the split metric of C and its complement. Tree networks, degree-one terminals and zero split weights are allowed. Nonterminal boundary vertices can be placed topologically inside the disk without changing the terminal order. Forcey's response matrix has the opposite sign from our Lambda; the resistance metric itself is unchanged.

Let Q be the incidence matrix of the positively weighted diameter edges, with an orientation to be fixed below, and put z_C=Q^T 1_C. Since Q^T 1=0,
\[
K:=Q^T RQ=-\tfrac12Q^TWQ
=\sum_Cw_Cz_Cz_C^T.
\]

## 3. A projectively ordered chord lemma

Orient every diameter chord into one common open half-plane and order their directions through that half-plane. Distinct diameter chords are nonparallel and any two intersect, with shared endpoints permitted. For three in order e<f<g and a circular terminal interval C, let z_h=1_C(head(h))-1_C(tail(h)). Then
\[
z_g(z_e-z_f)\le0,\qquad z_e(z_g-z_f)\le0. \tag{1}
\]

Here is the finite exact certificate and its geometric completeness argument. Three chords have at most six distinct endpoints. Removing all other vertices restricts a circular interval to a circular interval. Thus only strictly convex polygons with three through six vertices are needed.

The space of strictly convex labeled polygons with fixed cyclic orientation is connected. To verify this, place an interior point at the origin and write p_i=r_i u_i, with consecutive angular gaps delta_i in (0,pi). The strict-turn condition, divided by the product of the three consecutive radii, is
\[
\frac{\sin\delta_{i-1}}{r_{i+1}}
+\frac{\sin\delta_i}{r_{i-1}}
-\frac{\sin(\delta_{i-1}+\delta_i)}{r_i}>0.
\]
It is linear in the reciprocal radii. Interpolate them to a common positive constant; the endpoint satisfies all inequalities because it is a circular polygon. Consecutive edges remain in their disjoint angular sectors, so simplicity and strict convexity persist. On the resulting circle, interpolate the positive gaps to equal gaps. This connects to a regular polygon.

During such a deformation, pairwise-intersecting chords cannot become parallel: crossing endpoints stay alternating, and shared-endpoint chords would require three collinear strictly convex vertices. Their cyclic projective direction order therefore remains unchanged. Moving the direction cut cyclically rotates the order and reverses every chord wrapped across the cut. Global orientation reversal does not affect (1).

For each endpoint count use the strictly convex representative p_i=(i,i^2). A forward chord ij has slope i+j. Enumerate the pairwise-intersecting triples, sort by that slope, test their three cyclic cuts with wrapped orientations reversed, and test every circular interval. The independently implemented integer-only [certificate](erdos99-projective-chord-sign-certificate.json) tests 20,574 distinct interval/cut cases, finding exactly 19 sign triples and no failure of (1). Counting empty and full intervals once for every starting vertex gives 27,252 cases, matching the source's redundant count. The reproducible implementation is work/check-projective-chord-signs.py.

Summing (1) with the nonnegative resistance split weights yields the Robinson inequalities
\[
K_{eg}\le\min(K_{ef},K_{fg})\qquad(e<f<g). \tag{2}
\]

## 4. The weighted Robinson matrix lemma

Suppose L is symmetric, L1=Lt=0 for a strictly increasing vector t, and its off-diagonal entries are
\[
L_{ij}=-\gamma_i\gamma_j s_{ij},\qquad \gamma_i>0,
\]
where s satisfies the inequalities (2). Individual s entries may have either sign. Then L is positive semidefinite.

For completeness, let Gamma=diag(gamma), A0=Gamma^(-1)L, D0 the consecutive-difference matrix, and T0 the cumulative-sum map with (T0y)_j=sum_{r<j}y_r. Then D0 T0=I and T0 D0=I-1 e_1^T. The induced quotient matrix H=D0 A0 T0 has off-diagonal entries
\[
H_{ir}=\sum_{j>r}\gamma_j(s_{ij}-s_{i+1,j})\le0\quad(r>i),
\]
and, using zero row sums,
\[
H_{ir}=\sum_{j\le r}\gamma_j(s_{i+1,j}-s_{ij})\le0\quad(r<i).
\]
Also H(D0t)=0, with D0t strictly positive. Conjugation by diag(D0t) gives a matrix with zero row sums and nonpositive off-diagonal entries. Its Gershgorin disks lie in the closed right half-plane. Its spectrum is that of A0 modulo constants. But A0 is similar to the symmetric matrix Gamma^(-1/2)L Gamma^(-1/2). Its eigenvalues are therefore real and nonnegative. Congruence proves L>=0. No strictness or irreducibility is needed.

## 5. Assemble the universal stress matrix

Let Beta=diag(lambda)>0 on the positive diameter edges, and let X be the terminal coordinate matrix. Harmonic elimination of equilibrium gives
\[
\Lambda X=Q\,\mathrm{Beta}\,Q^TX.
\]
Put U=Q^TX. Multiplication by Q^T Lambda^+ yields
\[
K\,\mathrm{Beta}\,U=U. \tag{3}
\]
Choose a generic coordinate covector positive on every oriented chord, and an independent second coordinate. Then
\[
U=E[\mathbf1,t],\qquad E=\operatorname{diag}(a),\quad a_e>0,
\]
with t strictly increasing in the same projective order used in Section 3. It is essential to use the same oriented Q throughout.

The symmetric matrix
\[
M=E(\mathrm{Beta}-\mathrm{Beta}\,K\,\mathrm{Beta})E
\]
annihilates 1 and t by (3), and has off-diagonal entries -gamma_e gamma_f K_ef, where gamma_e=a_e lambda_e>0. Section 4 gives M>=0. Its congruence factorization gives
\[
\mathrm{Beta}^{-1}-Q^T\Lambda^+Q\succeq0.
\]
On the complement of constants set V=Lambda^(-1/2) Q Beta^(1/2). The displayed inequality is V^T V<=I, hence VV^T<=I. Congruence yields Lambda-Q Beta Q^T>=0. This is exactly the Schur complement of B-A in its positive definite interior block. Therefore B-A>=0.

If S is collinear, exposedness leaves exactly two terminals. The positive network lies on their segment and is a straight unit chain with D integer edges. Normalization gives contact weight D and diameter weight 1. The inequality reduces to
\[
D\sum_{j=0}^{D-1}(f_{j+1}-f_j)^2-(f_D-f_0)^2\ge0,
\]
which is Cauchy-Schwarz. Zero rows outside T are harmless. This completes universal positivity.

## 6. Finite release of unsupported active constraints

At a fixed configuration use exact signed quadratic inequalities g(x)=A0 x+q(x)>=0 on the strongly supported active rows: unit-contact signs are positive, diameter signs negative, and x is displacement. By maximal support, every nonnegative left-null vector of A0 is a physical stress after normalization; a contact-only one is excluded by evaluating equilibrium on dilation. Universal positivity gives
\[
\eta^Tq(x)\ge0\quad\text{for every }x
\]
for each such eta.

For any x, Farkas therefore makes A0 y>=-g(x) feasible. The fixed-matrix [Hoffman bound](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1905.02894) supplies a solution with
\[
\|y\|\le H\varepsilon(x),\qquad \varepsilon(x)=\|[g(x)]_-\|,
\]
where H depends on A0, not on the feasible right-hand side. Because q is quadratic,
\[
\varepsilon(x+y)\le L\bigl(H\|x\|\varepsilon(x)+H^2\varepsilon(x)^2\bigr).
\]
Start at x0=t v, with A0v=0. Its residual is C t^2. For t sufficiently small, successive corrections halve the residual, stay at norm O(t), and have total norm at most 2HCt^2. They converge to an actual feasible displacement
\[
x(t)=t v+O(t^2).
\]
This is a convergent finite-motion construction, not just a second-order jet. A maximal-support strict opener, proved in the path/cross document, has strictly favorable first-order signs on every unsupported full contact and actual diameter. Those signs survive the O(t^2) corrections, while inactive pairs retain their finite gaps. Thus every unsupported active row can be released simultaneously at fixed diameter.

## 7. Lexicographic normalization and the forest consequence

Among triangle-free global minimizers, select one minimizing its full unit-contact count and then its actual diameter-pair count. These minima exist as minima of nonempty sets of nonnegative integers; compactness of the triangle-free subset is unnecessary. If any active row were universally unsupported, Section 6 would produce a nearby unit-separated configuration with diameter at most D, no new active pairs, and strictly fewer contacts or, at the second stage, fewer diameter pairs. Global optimality preserves diameter D. This contradicts selection.

Consequently, this selected representative has a physical certificate positive on every full unit contact and every actual diameter pair. Its full unit graph has one nontrivial connected positive component, together with possible contact-isolated, diameter-free points. The isolated points have not been discarded.

The same integer selection can be performed inside an open ordinary-local-minimum neighborhood, at the same minimum value D. Take the neighborhood small enough that no old noncontact can become a contact. Its selected point is still an ordinary local minimum, and the same finite release forces full positive support.

Suppose the starting packing is triangle-free and its full contact graph is a forest. The selected graph is still a forest. The positive-tree loaded-leaf theorem then makes every actual diameter endpoint a full contact leaf. The previously checked full-leaf local theorem, applied to the entire packing including isolates, gives D<2 and n<=6. Therefore
\[
\boxed{\text{No triangle-free ordinary local diameter minimum with }n\ge7
\text{ has a full contact forest.}}
\]
More generally, an ordinary local minimum with n>=7 cannot have a maximal positive contact support that is a tree: release its unsupported full contacts first, obtaining a nearby same-diameter ordinary local minimum with full contact forest, then apply the preceding conclusion.

This eliminates maximal positive trees from the large local-minimum class. It does not eliminate positive cyclic blocks, interior isolated points, or all possible triangle-free global minimizers.

# Erdős #99: checked partial results

Research begun 25 October 2026. **No proof or disproof of Erdős #99 has been established.** These notes record restricted results and obstructions, with session attribution and no claim of literature novelty. The accompanying research log records failed approaches and pending audits.

**Latest checked frontier (28 October):** §§95–125 contain the universal stress/finite-release reductions, large-core geometry, global population reserve, all-population defect budgets and checked local countermodels. §§126–140 add exact finite reference classifications, an explicit even perturbation radius, sharpened endpoint lattice bounds, three-anchor/four-terminal topology, and local exchange/phase inequalities. The global cyclic-core/inactive-population gap remains. No proof or disproof has been established.

For n ≥ 2, let D_n be the minimum diameter of n distinct planar points with pairwise separation at least 1. A minimizer exists by compactness after anchoring one point and using any finite comparison bound. Its minimum separation is exactly 1, since otherwise uniform contraction improves it. The target is an eventual statement about **every global minimizer**. Local minima, affine optima, and near-minimizers are distinct notions.

## 1. Triangle-free configurations have infimum D_n for every fixed n

Take any optimizer and rotate one unit pair horizontally. Apply T_t(x,y)=(x,(1+t)y), t>0. Every distance weakly increases, the chosen pair stays unit, and a transformed distance can equal 1 only if it was a horizontal unit distance originally. Every surviving unit edge is horizontal, so the new configuration is triangle-free. Its diameter is at most (1+t)D_n.

Consequently the infimum diameter of triangle-free configurations is D_n. It need not be attained. There is no positive diameter gap even for fixed n. A stronger generic-perturbation argument makes all pair distances distinct before normalizing, producing near-minimizers with exactly one unit contact.

Attribution: elementary stretch argument developed by root and independently supplied by browser worker 05; generic perturbation supplied independently by several first-wave workers. Both arguments were directly checked.

## 2. A local minimum has nonparallel diametral pairs when n ≥ 3

Suppose first D>1 and all diametral pairs are horizontal. A sufficiently small vertical stretch preserves their lengths and keeps every other pair strictly shorter than D. As in §1, every surviving unit edge is horizontal. Their graph consists of disjoint paths and isolated vertices, and hence admits signs σ_i∈{−1,1} opposite across every unit edge.

From the stretched positions (x_i,y_i), set

q_i(ε)=(sqrt(1−ε²)x_i, y_i+(ε/2)σ_i).

A former unit edge has squared length (1−ε²)+ε²=1. All noncontact lower inequalities retain strict slack for sufficiently small ε. Every former diameter has squared length at most

(1−ε²)D²+ε² = D²−ε²(D²−1)<D².

All other upper inequalities retain strict slack. Both perturbations can be chosen arbitrarily small, contradicting local minimality. If no unit contact survives the first stretch, normalize immediately to obtain a strict improvement.

If D=1 and n≥3, planar unit separation permits only an equilateral triangle, which already has nonparallel diametral pairs. The two-point unit segment is the necessary exception.

Attribution: root developed a chain-bending proof; native verifier `/root/audit_unique_diameter` supplied a detailed audit. Browser worker 11 independently supplied the shorter alternating-sign compression above. No integer-diameter counterexample route remains under the unique-diameter hypothesis.

## 3. Exclusively parallel unit contacts cannot give a local minimum when D>1

Rotate all unit contacts horizontally and color their path components by σ_i∈{−1,1}, opposite on each unit edge. Choose 2/D²<c<2. Choose K>0 sufficiently large that, for each nonhorizontal diametral difference (a,b) and sign difference d=σ_i−σ_j, Kb²>bd. There are only finitely many such pairs.

Use the path

p_i(t)=((1−ct²)x_i, (1−Kt)y_i+tσ_i).

A former unit edge has squared length

(1−ct²)²+4t² = 1+(4−2c)t²+c²t⁴>1.

A horizontal diameter has squared length D²+(d²−2cD²)t²+O(t⁴)<D², because d²≤4<2cD². A nonhorizontal diameter decreases at first order, with derivative 2b(d−Kb)<0. Every other pair retains its strict lower and upper slack for sufficiently small t. Normalize afterward if minimum separation is greater than 1.

Thus every exact optimizer with n≥4 has nonparallel unit contacts. This does not force a contact triangle.

Attribution: browser worker 12; full formula and inequalities checked by root.

## 4. Exact optimal infinite density need not produce any unit triangle

Let h=sqrt(3)/2, f(j)=j/(1+|j|), and ε>0. Set

X_ε={(i+j/2, hj+εf(j)): i,j∈Z}.

For different rows, strict monotonicity of f makes the vertical separation exceed h times the row-index difference. ## 5. The unit square is the only triangle-free local minimum in the complete convex rhombic-tiling class

## 7. Triangle-free local minima can have the optimal leading density constant

B_m=sΛ∩closed_disk(0,R−2), A_m=P_m∪B_m.

The regular odd unit polygon is a local minimum of own diameter under unit separation. To see this, use Reinhardt's sharp perimeter inequality for a convex m-gon K:

per(K)≤2m·diam(K)·sin(π/(2m)).

One elementary proof is to take Q=K−K. Its perimeter is 2per(K), it has at most 2m sides, and it lies in the disk of radius diam(K). Jensen's inequality on successive central angles bounds its perimeter by 4m·diam(K)·sin(π/(2m)). This proves the displayed inequality. The regular odd polygon attains equality.

Sufficiently small labeled perturbations of the m boundary vertices preserve their strict convexity and cyclic order. Every adjacent side remains at least 1, so their perimeter remains at least m. The sharp inequality forces their diameter to remain at least L. This applies to the boundary subset of any sufficiently small feasible perturbation of all of A_m. Hence A_m is a genuine local diameter minimum in unrestricted configuration space.

It is **not a strict local minimum**: its interior points have slack in every incident lower and upper constraint and can move within a small product neighborhood with unchanged diameter.

Reattaching an isolated point adds one edge between components, preserving β, and improves one of the later criteria; hence q=0. Any actual contact-loss deformation that breaks a cyclic edge without new contacts lowers β and is forbidden. In particular, a contact-bar flex fixing every diameter vector must assign equal velocities along every cyclic edge: otherwise its straight-line motion opens that edge quadratically, with all other inequalities retained by finite slack. This does not freeze arbitrary bridges or guarantee positive stress on every frozen edge.

There is also a bridge restriction. In this selected configuration, a contact bridge whose two endpoints each have contact degree at least two must lie on a cycle after diametral edges are added. No vertex becomes isolated, so β and q stay fixed while m+q decreases, a contradiction.

Consequently, a contact component containing no diametral endpoint must be a star K_(1,t), 1≤t≤5. A cycle in such a component contradicts cyclic freezing by infinitesimally rotating the component. ## 16. An exact margin formulation of the unresolved quantifier

For n≥3 and δ≥0 let D_n(δ) be the minimum diameter of a unit-separated labeled configuration such that every triple has at least one pair at distance at least 1+δ. The constraints are closed; a collinear comparison and anchoring one point give compactness and attainment. Dilation of an unconstrained optimizer gives

D_n≤D_n(δ)≤(1+δ)D_n.

On the compact set M_n of anchored unconstrained global optimizers define

ρ_n=max_{X∈M_n} min_{|T|=3}[max_{i,j∈T}|x_i−x_j|−1].

The continuous maximum is attained, and

D_n(δ)=D_n if and only if 0≤δ≤ρ_n.

Indeed equality gives a constrained global optimizer whose triple margin is at least δ; conversely an optimizer attaining ρ_n is feasible for every such δ. Therefore ρ_n>0 if and only if SOME global optimizer is triangle-free. Erdős #99 asks whether ρ_n=0 for every sufficiently large n. This formulation makes clear why an infimum argument, a vanishing sequence of triangle margins, or fixed-n algebraic decidability cannot establish the eventual exact statement.

## 17. A uniform hull bound for small lattice errors and nearly maximal area

h=O_C(D(ρ+D^(−1/3))^(1/3))=o(D).

Only hull vertices need lattice approximation; neither triangle-freeness nor optimality is required for this geometric lemma.

Proof. The difference body Q=K−K lies in the radius-D disk and has area at least 4area(K), by Brunn–Minkowski. Its disk-area deficit E is at most 4CD. If its support function in a unit direction is D−t, the omitted cap has area at least (4/3)sqrt(D)t^(3/2), since 0≤t≤D. Thus t≤t_*=(3C)^(2/3)D^(1/3). Every supporting-face point x with normal u satisfies

|x−D u|²≤2D t_*=O_C(D^(4/3)).

For an interval I of outward normals of width δ≤1, all corresponding boundary points have tangent projection at most D sin(δ/2)+sqrt(2D t_*) in absolute value. Those edges form one consecutive chain, whose consistent tangent projection is at least cos(δ/2) times its length. Telescoping therefore bounds their total length by O_C(Dδ+D^(2/3)). In the plane the boundary-length measures of convex polygons add under Minkowski sum: parallel supporting-face lengths add. Hence the same bound holds for K, because S_Q(I)=S_K(I)+S_(−K)(I).

Choose lattice approximants λ_a for hull vertices. A hull edge e=b−a has |e|≥1 and differs from the nonzero lattice vector z=λ_b−λ_a by at most 2ρ. For ρ≤1/8, its direction is within O(ρ) of z's direction, in an angular sector of width at most one. Minimum lattice spacing gives O(R²) possible vectors z when |e|≤R, uniformly even for anisotropic lattices. The sector bound therefore controls the total length, and hence number, of short hull edges by O_C(R²(Dρ+D^(2/3))). Long edges number at most πD/R. Thus, for R≥2,

h≤C_C R²(Dρ+D^(2/3))+πD/R.

## 19. Positive contact stress is connected, and the diameter-pair bound improves to D/2

In any finite unit-separated planar packing of diameter D>1 carrying a nonnegative normalized contact/diameter equilibrium stress, its positive-contact graph has exactly ONE nontrivial component. It contains every endpoint of every positive-weight diametral pair, and therefore has diameter exactly D. Triangle-freeness and optimality are not assumptions of this stress-connectivity statement.

Proof. The virial identity gives Σμ=D²Σλ=D²>0. Every positive-diameter endpoint is incident to a positive contact: any two norm-D displacements based at the same point have dot product at least D²/2, so a nonempty nonnegative diameter load cannot cancel there. Conversely every nontrivial positive-contact component contains a loaded endpoint, by its component virial identity.

Loaded endpoints are vertices of the overall convex hull. Partition them by positive-contact components. This is a NONCROSSING partition in their cyclic convex order: distinct components have disjoint planar unit-contact paths, which cannot connect alternating boundary endpoints. A noncrossing partition with at least two blocks has a proper interval block. For example, cut the cyclic order anywhere and choose a block with minimum linear span; any block entering the interior of that span must be contained there, contradicting minimality unless the chosen block is consecutive.

The convex hull of that interval block is strictly separated from all remaining loaded vertices. Sum equilibrium over its contact component. Internal contact and diameter forces cancel. Every outgoing positive-diameter force has strictly the same projection sign across the separating line, so there can be NO such outgoing force. The component virial identity now forces an INTERNAL positive-weight diameter pair.

Any other positive-contact component has a loaded endpoint. Since no positive diameter force exits the selected interval component, another positive diameter pair has BOTH endpoints outside that interval block. The selected component's internal diameter pair has both endpoints inside the block. The two pairs cannot alternate cyclically, whereas two diameter segments with four distinct endpoints must cross and hence alternate. This is a contradiction. For completeness, if two diameter segments were noncrossing opposite sides of a convex quadrilateral, strict triangle inequalities at the intersection of its diagonals would give 2D<sum of the diagonal lengths≤2D. The collinear case has a unique diameter pair and follows directly from component equilibrium and the virial identity. An equivalent proof peels off interval components one at a time; each removed component retains an internal diameter pair, giving the same contradiction.

There is consequently just one positive-contact component, and all positively loaded endpoints belong to it, as claimed.

Apply this at B in §18. One full contact component has diameter D, so Σℓ_j≥2D. The same independently checked minimal-contact rank and triangle-free Euler count now give the stronger conclusion

Interpolate velocities affinely along each compressed bar. Reverse this velocity and integrate it exactly. For each oriented compressed bar with vector r, length L and relative velocity h, set
